source.title: Improving Deep Transformer with Depth-Scaled Initialization and Merged Attention
source.authors: Biao Zhang; Ivan Titov; R. Sennrich

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether initialization and depth affect gradient flow and trainability in deep Transformer models, using gradient norms, training-set metrics, and translation outcomes rather than the claim’s CIFAR classification error measure.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own deep-Transformer gradient, training-set BLEU/perplexity, and depth results. Translation BLEU and perplexity are not classification error; they do not establish near-zero training classification error. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures initialization-dependent gradient flow and trainability in residual, layer-normalized Transformers. V4 specifies activation-matched initialization in plain networks and particular orthogonal-initialization results; this study tests depth-scaled initialization in a different architecture. It also does not test the convolutional-network, teacher-student, stability-threshold, or batch-normalization conditions of the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors attribute deep Transformer convergence problems to gradient vanishing from residual connections followed by layer normalization, mitigate this with DS-Init, and combine it with MAtt to improve translation quality while approximately preserving baseline decoding speed. Models train successfully up to 30 layers per side, with relatively small gains beyond 12 layers.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses depth-scaled initialization in Transformer translation models and evaluates gradients, translation metrics, and training dynamics. The original claim concerns image classification training error on CIFAR datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: Gradient behavior and optimization depend on applying DS-Init to both encoder and decoder; one-sided use led to instability. Depth gains were steepest from 6 to 12 layers and relatively small beyond 12.

fits_no_version.finding: DS-Init reduces gradient attenuation and stabilizes training in post-normalization residual Transformers; applying it to only the encoder or decoder causes instability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth-scaled initialization can improve gradient propagation and trainability in deep post-normalization encoder-decoder Transformers, with successful application depending on initializing both sides.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep DS-Init models train successfully, and DS-Init+MAtt models reach 30 layers per side with diminishing translation gains beyond 12 layers. Training-set fitting and development BLEU favor different variants.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Appropriate initialization enables deeper residual Transformers, while translation generalization gains need not track improved training-set fitting.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The study does not measure classification error; training-set BLEU and perplexity are different outcomes. Gradient norm plots do not report exact numeric values. The flattened Table 4 text makes some model-ID mappings uncertain, and no uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported training metrics.

untested.parts: CIFAR convolutional-network training classification error, including random or corrupted labels and the stated model-size and training-recipe conditions.
Spurious local minima and student overparameterization in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation in plain convolutional networks versus identity-shortcut networks, and the specified tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization and learning speed or trainable depth in plain networks; orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh initialization; orthogonal convolution kernels at 10,000 layers.
Above-threshold learning rates, catapult dynamics, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability training, and below-threshold divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons and normalization-free residual training using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied claim versions, not assertions that the paper's Transformer effects are unreadable or absent. Table 3 additionally reports optimization failure for deep vanilla and MAtt-only Transformers, contrasted with successful DS-Init training; this is relevant to the proposed Transformer claim but does not supply a missing test of V1–V6. No external sources or files were accessed.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer comparison, and early stopping are not tested.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and student width relative to teacher width are not tested.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks and the effects of shortcuts, Fixup, or special initialization on classification training error are not tested.

The paper tests depth-scaled initialization in Transformer translation models. It does not test activation-matched initialization generally, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, tanh networks, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above a stability limit, loss-curvature changes, and edge-of-stability dynamics are not tested.
Batch normalization is not tested; the paper uses layer normalization and does not compare Fixup residual networks.

rows.subject: Transformer + DS-Init + MAtt
rows.operation_detail: Compared successful training and relative performance across depths.
rows.value: training was successful and improved over shallower counterparts; gains relatively small beyond 12 layers

rows.subject: Transformer with DS-Init on encoder only
rows.operation_detail: Applied DS-Init to encoder alone; optimization became unstable and gradients tended to explode.
rows.note: The encoder-only variant is unstable; gradient clipping yielded the stated BLEU, 0.66 BLEU below the full variant.
rows.check: One-sided DS-Init instability qualifies the proposed Transformer method, not V4's claims about plain networks.

rows.subject: Transformer with DS-Init on decoder only
rows.operation_detail: Applied DS-Init to decoder alone; optimization became unstable and gradients tended to explode.
rows.note: Paper explicitly states that clipping fails for decoder.
rows.check: Failure of decoder-only DS-Init and gradient clipping qualifies the proposed Transformer method, not a stated version.
